$comment: The implementations awr/conformance/run.py drives, as SPEC.md section 17 CLI descriptors.
A descriptor is a claim about a command, not about a codebase: run.py knows nothing of any
implementation's internals and speaks to all of them through the section 17 subcommands only.
Add a third-party implementation by appending a descriptor, or -- without touching this file --
by passing one on the command line:

$fields.name: Stable identifier; the column heading in the matrix and the key in results.json.
$fields.language: Implementation language and version, as the submitter states it.
$fields.cryptoLibrary: The Ed25519 and SHA-256 provider. Recorded because 'it verifies' is a claim about a crypto stack as much as about the code.
$fields.role: Free-form: what this implementation is for.
$fields.command: Argv prefix. Every element is placeholder-expanded (see $placeholders).
$fields.commandCandidates: Alternative argv prefixes, tried in order; the first whose executable exists is used. Use instead of 'command' when the same implementation is reachable by more than one path.
$fields.env: Environment variables to add for every invocation; values are placeholder-expanded.
$fields.runtimeVersionCommand: OPTIONAL, and NOT part of section 17: a command whose stdout identifies the runtime, recorded in results.json as provenance. ${IMPL_EXE} expands to the resolved command[0].
$fields.optionalSubcommands: Section 17 subcommands this implementation declares it does not provide. 'issue' is OPTIONAL for verify-only implementations; anything else here is a conformance gap, and run.py records it as such.
$fields.notes: Anything a reader of the matrix needs in order to interpret this row.

$placeholders.${REPO_ROOT}: The repository root (the parent of awr/).
$placeholders.${ANY_ENV_VAR}: Any other ${NAME} is taken from the environment; unset names expand to the empty string and are reported.

implementations.name: python-reference
implementations.cryptoLibrary: cryptography (PyCA) — Ed25519 and SHA-256 via OpenSSL
implementations.role: reference implementation; the vectors are generated by it, so a vector it fails is a bug in one of the two and never a tie-break
implementations.notes: Pure-Python RFC 8785 canonicalizer with a lexical number scanner (section 4.3); the only dependency is the Ed25519 primitive.

implementations.name: rust
implementations.role: independent implementation, written from SPEC.md without reading the Python source — the reason the spec had to say what it means
implementations.notes: Build with `cargo build --offline` in awr/rust. Emits compact JSON; section 17 constrains the payload, not its framing.

implementations.name: browser-node
implementations.cryptoLibrary: Node crypto (Ed25519, SHA-256); WebCrypto in the browser
implementations.role: the verifier that runs in the page at verify.modelmarket.dev, driven through a section 17 adapter so the code a stranger's browser executes is the code this matrix measures
implementations.notes: Verify-only: the page holds no private key, and section 17 makes `issue` OPTIONAL. `issue` exits 3, which run.py records as an absent optional capability and not as a failure.
